finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::read-only sql guard bypassable: validator strips "comments" the executed query does not have, allowing arbitrary multi-statement sql on the datasource feature this change newly documents/advertises
evidence: Verified in packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts:26-31: comment stripping (`--…` and `/*…*/`) is regex-only with no string-literal awareness, and every subsequent check (first token, FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS, semicolon/multi-statement) operates on the stripped text, while datasource.service.ts executes the *original* `dto.query` interpolated into `SELECT * FROM (${dto.query}) AS _q LIMIT …` via `client.query()` with no bind params (simple-query protocol → multiple statements allowed). A `/*` opened inside a string literal and closed by `*/` in a later literal blanks out the middle of the statement for the validator only, so `; DROP TABLE t;` or `COPY … FROM PROGRAM` in that region passes as `SELECT '' AS b`; the semicolon check can't see it either because the semicolons were deleted with the pseudo-comment. Access is gated only by JwtAuthGuard + assertMember (datasource.controller.ts executeQuery), so any workspace member can escalate the "read-only SELECT" tab into arbitrary DML/DDL against the connection owner's credentials. Pre-existing code, as the claim itself notes; the diff only adds docs/homepage copy advertising the read-only guarantee.
